proposals.evidence: DEDR 3507 directly gives Tamil tonti ‘large belly, abdomen’, alongside Malayalam tonti. The survey belly noun matches the printed word; the Sanskrit tunda comparison leaves the family’s deeper contact history open, so this is a lexical-family proposal rather than an asserted loan route.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 546 directly gives Tamil īral/īruḷ ‘internal organ, liver or spleen’, with Malayalam īral ‘liver’. The survey īraḷ ‘liver’ is proposed with its retroflex lateral preserved; no claim is made that all source uses denote liver exclusively.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1391 directly gives Tamil kaṟi ‘meat (raw or boiled)’, as well as vegetables and pepper. The survey kari ‘meat’ agrees with an explicit Tamil sense; it is not inferred from the narrower curry meaning in some other languages.
